Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the VitaHealth Hospitals, Inc. Third Quarter Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question, please press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then two. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss VitaHealth Hospitals' financial results for the third quarter. Joining me on the call are Michael Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Emily Patel, Chief Medical Officer; Tom Hargrove, Chief Operating Officer; Karen Walsh, Chief Strategy Officer; and Raj Singh, Chief Information Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that certain statements made during this call may contain forward-looking statements within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks, uncertainties, and other factors that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Michael Reynolds.

Michael Reynolds:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on our performance for the third quarter. We continue to execute on our strategic priorities, focusing on delivering high-quality patient care, expanding our network, and improving operational efficiency.

Today, I will provide an overview of our key achievements during the quarter, focusing on seven key aspects: our payer revenue mix, capital expenditure guidance for the coming periods, the impact of seasonality and external factors, labor costs as a percentage of revenue, factors affecting our operating margin, total admissions and patient days, and our revenue breakdown by service line.

Let me begin with our payer revenue mix, which remains a cornerstone of our operational strategy in the acute care hospital sector. It reflects the broader dynamics in the healthcare services industry—shifting reimbursement landscapes, payer negotiations, and post-pandemic volume recovery—while underscoring our disciplined approach to revenue cycle management and payer diversification. For the quarter ended September 30, 2023, our net patient revenue breakdown was Medicare at 42.1%, up 110 basis points sequentially from 41.0% in the second quarter. This represents about $1.2 billion of our total $2.85 billion in net revenue. Year-over-year, Medicare held steady from 41.8% in the third quarter of 2022, but we've seen a modest uptick driven by higher acuity inpatient volumes in our Medicare Advantage subset, which now comprises 28% of total Medicare revenue, up from 24% a year ago. This aligns with industry trends, as CMS data shows Medicare Advantage penetration exceeding 50% nationally, with plans like UnitedHealthcare and Humana aggressively expanding in our core markets.

Medicaid came in at 18.3%, flat sequentially but up 80 basis points year-over-year from 17.5%, equating to roughly $520 million. Our Medicaid strength continues in the Southeast, where we operate 14 of our 42 hospitals, benefiting from state expansions under the ACA and redeterminations post-pandemic unwind. For instance, in Florida and Georgia—key regions for us—Medicaid managed care rates have stabilized post the 2022-2023 rate hikes, with our average reimbursement per adjusted patient day up 4.2% year-over-year. We're actively bidding on new managed Medicaid contracts with Centene's WellCare and Molina, targeting a 20% mix by fiscal 2025.

Commercial insurance was 31.4%, down 120 basis points from 32.6% in the second quarter and 150 basis points softer year-over-year. This segment generated $895 million, reflecting margin pressure from escalating site-neutral payment policies and higher member deductibles amid medical loss ratio scrutiny. Blues plans like Anthem and Cigna represent 55% of our commercial book, and while we've locked in mid-single-digit rate increases for 2024 renewals—averaging 5.8%—outpatient shift to ambulatory surgery centers has tempered inpatient commercial growth. Our commercial case mix index of 1.85 remains above the HFMA median of 1.72, supporting premium pricing.

Self-pay and other, including charity care and uninsured, was 8.2%, up slightly from 7.9% in the second quarter due to seasonal elective procedures. This $235 million bucket is managed tightly through our enhanced revenue cycle tech stack, with self-pay collections at 42%—well above the 2023 MGMA benchmark of 35%. We've extended our partnership with R1 RCM for AI-driven denial management, reducing self-pay A/R days to 48 from 55 year-over-year.

Over the past three years, our payer mix has evolved from 40% Medicare, 19% Medicaid, 33% commercial, and 8% self-pay in fiscal 2021 to today's composition, with Medicare's share expanding amid the aging Baby Boomer cohort—projected by CMS to drive 10-15% inpatient growth through 2030. Medicaid's resilience post-redeterminations—we've retained 92% of our base—positions us well against peers like HCA Healthcare, whose Medicaid mix sits at 15%. However, commercial erosion—now at a three-year low—highlights the need for upside levers. Regionally, our Midwest footprint in Illinois and Ohio, with 18 hospitals, is Medicare-heavy at 48% mix, buoyed by strong SNF and home health transitions under MSSP ACO REACH, where we're tracking for $45 million in shared savings this year. The Southeast Medicaid tailwind offsets West Coast commercial softness, where California regs have capped our rates.

Technical initiatives driving optimization include our full Epic rollout across 85% of facilities, boosting charge capture accuracy to 98%, directly lifting Medicare DRG reimbursements by 3.1% year-over-year. In value-based care, 35% of Medicare revenue is now at risk through bundled payments and our narrow network with Humana Medicare Advantage, yielding 2x ROI on care navigation investments. AI-powered modeling via Change Healthcare tools informed 2024 contracts, securing 6-7% commercial uplifts and value-based adders tied to readmission rates—ours at 14.2% versus the 16.1% national average. For self-pay mitigation, we've expanded PromptPay discounts and integration with Experian Health for real-time eligibility checks, converting 25% more uninsured to insured at point-of-service. Looking forward, we expect payer mix stability in the fourth quarter with Medicare at 42-43%, Medicaid ticking to 18.5-19%, commercial steady at 31%, and self-pay moderating to 7.5-8%. Our strategy emphasizes commercial growth via employer-direct contracting—piloting with three Fortune 500 clients—and Medicaid managed care penetration, targeting a shift to 35/20/37/8% by 2026 for higher-margin stability. This positions VitaHealth to outperform amid CMS's 2.9% IPPS update and ongoing payer consolidation.

Moving to capital expenditure guidance for fiscal 2024 and beyond, capex remains a critical lever for us in the healthcare services and hospitals sector, where we're navigating shifting payer mix, regulatory tailwinds like the CMS FY2024 IPPS updates, and the transition from fee-for-service to value-based care. For full fiscal 2024, we are guiding capex to a range of $475 million to $525 million, representing approximately 4.8% to 5.3% of our projected revenue base of around $10.2 billion. This is a modest 5-8% increase from our 2023 actuals of $450 million, reflecting disciplined capital allocation amid elevated interest rates and construction costs up about 7% year-over-year per the Turner Building Cost Index for healthcare facilities. We prioritize return on invested capital, targeting projects with IRR hurdles above 12-15%, in line with peers like HCA Healthcare and Tenet Healthcare.

Breaking it down: Maintenance and regulatory capex is about 60% of total, or $285-315 million, including routine refreshes of our aging inpatient infrastructure across our 42-hospital footprint, primarily in the Southeast and Mid-Atlantic. Key spends are HVAC upgrades to comply with updated ASHRAE 170 ventilation standards post-COVID and seismic retrofits in our California facilities ahead of 2025 deadlines. Costs here are up 10-12% due to supply chain normalization, but we've locked in multi-year contracts with Trane and Cummins.

Growth and capacity expansion is around 25%, or $120-130 million. We're accelerating high-margin outpatient services, now 42% of procedural volumes. This quarter, we'll break ground on two new ambulatory surgery centers in Florida's Tampa-Orlando corridor, with combined capacity for 15,000 cases annually at 85% utilization, modeled after Tenet partnerships. Additionally, $40 million for de novo freestanding ERs in Texas exurbs, capitalizing on 15%+ EBITDA margins.

Technology and digital transformation is 15%, or $70-80 million, up 20% year-over-year. This includes $25 million for Epic MyChart enhancements and AI integrations, rolling out Epic's Cosmos AI across 80% of beds by year-end for predictive sepsis detection at 92% accuracy. $20 million in advanced imaging like Siemens NAEOTOM Alpha CT scanners and da Vinci Xi expansions to 25 ORs, targeting 15% robotic case mix lift. $15-20 million in cybersecurity with Palo Alto zero-trust and telehealth expansion to 40 sites.

For the fourth quarter specifically, expect $125-140 million, skewed toward ASC groundwork and Epic go-lives. This positions us for margin expansion to 8.5-9.0% adjusted EBITDA, driven by volume growth and tech productivity. We're holding $800 million dry powder for tuck-ins.

Next, on the impact of seasonality and external factors, particularly respiratory illness season with flu, RSV, and COVID variants, our same-hospital admissions grew robustly, driven by acute respiratory cases. Emergency department visits spiked, with inpatient admissions for pneumonia and influenza-like illnesses up significantly, lifting our case mix index and adding to net revenue per admission under Medicare's MS-DRG system. Total net patient revenue benefited substantially from these volumes.

However, variable labor and supply costs for antivirals escalated, with regional variations—sharpest in the Northeast, moderate in the Sunbelt. External factors like CDC-tracked flu severity amplified this, but our AI predictive analytics with Epic forecasted peaks accurately, reducing length of stay. Rapid diagnostics cut unnecessary admissions, and just-in-time inventory buffered shortages. Investments in virtual nursing will flatten future swings.

Turning to labor costs as a percentage of revenue, our largest expense at 57.4% this quarter, up 210 basis points year-over-year, totaling around $1.64 billion on a 9.2% increase. Driven by 7.5% wage rises and overtime at 4.2%, with RN wages at $48.50 per hour up 8.1%. Regional pressures highest in California at 62.1%, steadier in Southeast at 55.2%. Mitigation via Epic MyWorkforce reducing unproductive hours 12%, AI tools like Qventus improving NHPPD 15%, and upskilling programs. Expect peak at 57.8% next quarter, moderating to 56.5-57.0% full-year.

Factors affecting operating margin came in strong at 12.5%, up 230 basis points year-over-year, from 8.2% revenue growth outpacing 4.8% expense rise. Volumes up 5.1%, CMI 1.85, favorable commercial mix. Labor up only 5.2%, supplies deleveraged via GPO savings, bad debt improved. Headwinds like California wages offset by ASC shifts and ACO savings. Outlook 12.7-13.3% next quarter.

On total admissions and patient days, we delivered 128,500 admissions, up 4.8% YoY and 1.9% QoQ; 742,000 patient days, up 3.9% YoY and 1.2% QoQ, ALOS 5.77 days. Organic growth stronger, driven by electives, orthopedics up 12%. Regional strength in Southeast, tech like Nuance DAX boosting capacity 10%.

Finally, revenue breakdown: Acute inpatient 42% ($1.20B, +6.8% YoY), outpatient 28% ($798M, +14.5%), ED/observation 12% ($342M, +7.2%), surgical 10% ($285M, +12.1%), behavioral/other 8% ($228M, +9.3%). Outpatient fastest-growing, ASCs shining.

Now, I’ll turn the call over to Lisa Chen to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

Lisa Chen:
Thank you, Michael. Good morning, everyone. As Michael mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Net revenue for the third quarter was $2.85 billion, an increase of 8.2% compared to the same period last year. This growth was driven by increased patient volume, favorable payer mix, and the successful implementation of our revenue cycle management initiatives.

Our operating expenses were $2.42 billion, representing 85% of net revenue. We are continuing to focus on managing our costs effectively while investing in key growth initiatives, particularly in supply chain optimization.

Net income for the quarter was $285 million, or $2.10 per share. We are pleased with our financial performance and remain confident in our ability to achieve our financial goals for the year.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Emily Patel for an update on our clinical initiatives.

Dr. Emily Patel:
Thank you, Lisa. Good morning. We are making significant progress in improving clinical outcomes and patient satisfaction. Our Heart Failure Care Pathway program has shown promising results, with a 25% reduction in readmission rates. We are also focused on leveraging technology to enhance the patient experience and improve care coordination, specifically through our telehealth platform and remote patient monitoring programs.

Following that, Tom Hargrove will provide an update on operational efficiency.

Tom Hargrove:
Thank you, Dr. Patel. We are focused on streamlining our operations and improving efficiency across our network. We have implemented several initiatives, including AI-driven staffing optimization and centralized supply chain management, which have resulted in significant cost savings and improved patient flow.

Next, Karen Walsh will discuss our strategic initiatives.

Karen Walsh:
Thank you, Tom. Our strategic priorities remain focused on expanding our network, developing new partnerships, and investing in innovative technologies. We are actively exploring opportunities to grow our footprint in key markets and enhance our service offerings.

After that, Raj Singh will discuss our IT infrastructure and cybersecurity.

Raj Singh:
Thank you, Karen. We are committed to maintaining a robust and secure IT infrastructure to support our operations and protect patient data. We have implemented several new security measures to enhance our cybersecurity posture and ensure compliance with regulatory requirements.

Now, I'd like to turn the call back to Michael Reynolds.

Michael Reynolds:
Thank you, everyone. At this time, we will open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Our first question comes from David Lee with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

David Lee:
Good morning. Can you discuss the impact of the recent cybersecurity threats on your operations and patient data?

Raj Singh:
Good morning, David. Thank you for the question. Recent cybersecurity threats, including the Change Healthcare incident, have heightened industry vigilance, but at VitaHealth, we've experienced no material disruptions to operations or patient data breaches. Our proactive investments—$15-20 million this year in Palo Alto Networks zero-trust architecture—have fortified our defenses, achieving 99.9% uptime across Epic systems. We've segmented networks per NIST frameworks, conducted quarterly penetration testing with Mandiant, and achieved HITRUST CSF certification at 95% of facilities. Patient data remains secure, with PHI encryption at rest and in transit, and our incident response time under 4 hours. This positions us ahead of peers, with zero regulatory fines YTD. We're also collaborating with HHS on sector-wide resilience sharing.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Jennifer Kim with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Jennifer Kim:
What are your plans for expanding your telehealth capabilities and remote patient monitoring programs?

Dr. Emily Patel:
Thanks, Jennifer. Great question. We're aggressively scaling telehealth and RPM, building on 300% volume growth last year. Our Apex Virtual Care platform—now at 40 sites with 5G RPM for CHF patients—will expand to all 42 hospitals by mid-2024, targeting 20% of post-acute encounters remotely. This aligns with Optum's value-based push, reducing readmissions 25% in pilots via wearables integrated with Epic. Partnerships with Philips for tele-ICU add 15% capacity in rural sites, and AI triage via Nuance DAX cuts ED diversions 18%. Expect $50 million revenue uplift in 2024, with 28% EBITDA margins from lower ALOS.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mark Thompson with Bank of America. Please go ahead.

Mark Thompson:
Can you provide more details on your strategic partnerships and their potential impact on your business?

Karen Walsh:
Thanks, Mark. Our partnerships are core to growth. Recent ACO REACH with Humana targets $45 million shared savings, covering 1.2 million lives at 35% risk. Employer-direct pilots with three Fortune 500s shift commercial mix to 37% by 2026. ASC joint ventures like Tenet models in Florida add 15,000 cases, and Vizient GPO yields 11% supply savings. Tempus AI for oncology precision boosts CMI 150 bps. Impact: 2-3% volume growth, 200 bps margin expansion, positioning for $10B+ revenue.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Alex Rivera with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thanks. On capex, how are you prioritizing amid high interest rates, and any M&A updates?

Lisa Chen:
Hi Alex. Capex at $475-525M for 2024 prioritizes 12-15% IRR projects: 60% maintenance like HVAC/seismic, 25% growth in ASCs/ERs, 15% tech like AI/Epic. Fixed-rate debt gives flexibility; $800M dry powder for $200-400M tuck-ins, eyeing Midwest like UHS deals. No major M&A Q4, but pipeline strong for 2025.

Michael Reynolds:
Thank you for the questions. In closing, I want to thank our dedicated employees for their hard work and commitment to providing high-quality care to our patients. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and delivering long-term value to our shareholders.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you for your participation in today's call. This concludes the VitaHealth Hospitals Third Quarter Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
